claim:
PR title: fix(apps-mcp): a restart waits for in-flight app deploys instead of killing them

## Why
An apply that recreates `apps-mcp` sent SIGTERM and the process exited at once, killing an app build in progress (roadmap-keeper deploy #209, 2026-11-16: failed, auto-rolled back, owner alerted; ~5 min degraded).

## What
- `deploy.ts`: the engine's `exclusive` section (deploy, rollback, preview, run, remove) refuses new work once `drain()` is called, and `drain(ms)` resolves when the in-flight ones finish or after `ms`.
- `main.ts`: SIGTERM/SIGINT drain for up to 10 minutes, then exit.
- `loops.ts` / `previews.ts`: the reconcile and preview ticks skip while draining, so a refused deploy is never paged or recorded as a failed preview.
- `compose.yaml`: `stop_grace_period: 11m` on `apps-mcp` (`docker compose up` recreates with SIGTERM and waits that long, so the apply simply takes longer while a deploy finishes).
- Test: SIGTERM-style drain waits for a deploy mid-`compose up`, refuses new deploys, and the deploy ends healthy.

Not done: retrying a deploy that is SIGKILLed anyway (needs an in-progress marker and a startup retry); drain timeout is the backstop. The apply does not log "waiting for N deploys" (it cannot see them without an apps-mcp call).

Tests: apps-mcp `npm test && npm run typecheck` pass. Lean: trusted +18 (33583 to 33601, baseline 33611).
